base: clusters-v2.md (38 clusters: 23 kept or updated from the 2026-11-13 run, 13 new, 2 gaps found in the old digests)
selection: Greedy over new-cluster coverage, one digest per concern, nine digests.

digests.why: The parent of the readability review. It states the group split, the coverage proof against git ls-files, the negative control, and the rule that a child which searched instead of reading is sent back.
One of eight verification children, and the one that corrects citations, refuses an unactionable glossary finding, and labels a required approval as a proposed rule.
A fix child over the research records. It states the historical-record rule, the do-not-guess rule, the fixed/open report, and the parallel edit boundary.
The PR #74 review. It probes host tool versions, force-pushes with a lease, previews the rebase with git merge-tree, and rejects four quoted outputs that no record holds.
The ADR 0010 fix after a rebase. The person's words are the rule: re-validate the findings, then fix them, and re-run the gate the rebase changed.

The frontier spawn session. It states the branch prefix by ticket type, the model switch that must reach every remaining spawn, and the goal for a grilling ticket. Its lessons belong to the global hwt skill, so it also tests whether a model files them in the wrong repository.
The property-test session. It states the oracle-from-contract rule, the failure proof against pre-fix code, and the separate commit.
The rename request. It states the host state a rename strands and the down-then-up order, which retire-a-name does not.
The nested-LXD wrapup. It states that future work is captured in extant or new tickets when a research ticket closes.
